## Statute

§1. Tax imposed (lines 1-17):

(a) Married individuals filing joint returns and surviving spouses

There is hereby imposed on the taxable income of-

    (1) every married individual (as defined in section 7703) who makes a single return jointly with his spouse, and

    (2) every surviving spouse (as defined in section 2(a)),

a tax determined in accordance with the following:

    (i) 15% of taxable income if the taxable income is not over $36,900;
    (ii) $5,535, plus 28% of the excess over $36,900 if the taxable income is over $36,900 but not over $89,150;
    (iii) $20,165, plus 31% of the excess over $89,150 if the taxable income is over $89,150 but not over $140,000;
    (iv) $35,928.50, plus 36% of the excess over $140,000 if the taxable income is over $140,000 but not over $250,000;
    (v) $75,528.50, plus 39.6% of the excess over $250,000 if the taxable income is over $250,000.

§151. Allowance of deductions for personal exemptions, subsection (d)(1) (lines 68-72):

For purposes of this section-

    (1) In general

    Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the term "exemption amount" means $2,000.

§152. Dependent defined, subsection (c)(1)(B) (line 127):

        (B) who has the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of such taxable year,

§152. Dependent defined, subsection (c)(3) (lines 142-144):

    For purposes of paragraph (1)(C), an individual meets the requirements of this paragraph if such individual is younger than the taxpayer claiming such individual as a qualifying child and is less than 25 years old at the end of the taxable year.

§153. Standard deduction, subsection (a)(2) (lines 386-396):

    (2) Basic standard deduction

    For purposes of paragraph (1), the basic standard deduction is-

        (A) 200 percent of the dollar amount in effect under subparagraph (C) for the taxable year in the case of-

            (i) a joint return, or

            (ii) a surviving spouse (as defined in section 2(a)),

        (B) $4,400 in the case of a head of household (as defined in section 2(b)), or

        (C) $3,000 in any other case.

## Reasoning

1. Filing status: Alice files a joint return with her spouse (case fact: "Alice files a joint return with her spouse for 2015"). Under §1(a), this falls under "Married individuals filing joint returns and surviving spouses."

2. Gross income: $42,876 (case fact: "Alice's and her spouse's gross income for the year 2015 is $42876").

3. Standard deduction: Under §153(a)(2)(A), the basic standard deduction for a joint return is 200 percent of $3,000 (from §153(a)(2)(C)) = $6,000.

4. Exemptions: Under §151(d)(1), the exemption amount is $2,000. Alice is entitled to:
   - An exemption for herself (taxpayer)
   - An exemption for her spouse (joint return filer)
   - An exemption for Bob (her son, who has the same principal place of abode as her per §152(c)(1)(B) at line 127)
   
   Charlie is NOT Alice's dependent because Charlie's principal place of abode is with Bob (his father), not Alice. Under §152(c)(1)(B), a qualifying child must have the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer.
   
   Total exemptions = 3 × $2,000 = $6,000.

5. Note on age requirements: §152(c)(3) (lines 142-144) requires a qualifying child to be younger than the taxpayer and less than 25 years old at the end of the taxable year. The case facts do not provide ages for Bob or Charlie, so this requirement cannot be verified from the facts provided.

6. Taxable income computation (lines 360-362): Taxable income = Gross income - Standard deduction - Exemptions
   = $42,876 - $6,000 - $6,000 = $30,876

7. Tax calculation: Under §1(a)(i), since taxable income ($30,876) is not over $36,900, the tax is 15% of taxable income.
   Tax = 15% × $30,876 = $4,631.40, rounded to whole number = $4,631.
